title: Jinnahs Fourteen Points Demand 1929
definition: A charter of demands issued by Muhammad Ali Jinnah in March 1929 as a counter-proposal to the Nehru Report (1928), outlining the minimum political safeguards required by the Muslim League for participation in a future constitutional framework.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the 'Parting of Ways' between the Congress and the Muslim League, the evolution of communal politics, and the transition from constitutional agitation to the demand for separate electorates.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Jinnahs Fourteen Points Demand 1929.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
